brief:
You are writing test material for a benchmark. Do not read or run anything; just answer.

Context: people dictate long, rambling voice messages to a coding assistant (some in Brazilian Portuguese, some in English). Each message holds one main request buried among side errands, background and thinking aloud.

Write four lists of short spoken phrases:

1. "marker_pt" and "marker_en": 10 phrases each that a speaker says right before the single most important request of the message, to flag it as the main one. The request follows the phrase directly in the same sentence.
2. "restate_pt" and "restate_en": 10 phrases each that a speaker uses near the end of the message to open a short closing recap that repeats the main request. The repeated request follows the phrase directly in the same sentence.

Rules for every phrase:
- Natural spoken register: colloquial Brazilian Portuguese for the _pt lists, casual spoken English for the _en lists.
- Vary the wording: no two phrases in a list built around the same key word.
- End with ": " or ", " (colon or comma, then one space); the request is appended right after, starting with a lowercase letter.
- No other sentence-ending punctuation (no . ! ? or ellipsis) and no line breaks, quotation marks, emoji or dashes.
- At most 12 words. Do not start with a negation. Do not include the request itself.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"marker_pt": [...], "marker_en": [...], "restate_pt": [...], "restate_en": [...]}

marker_pt: o que eu mais preciso de você é:
a parte que realmente importa é:
se for pra resolver uma coisa só, é:
marker_en: what I really need you to do is:
above all, I want you to:
the part that matters most is:
if you only tackle one thing:
put this at the top of the list:
restate_pt: no fim das contas, eu preciso disso:
restate_en: bringing it back to the main point:
